transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. It's really nice to meet you too. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. Um, I guess I'm here because... well, I've been having a little trouble with my words lately. It's probably nothing major, but I just want to make sure I'm explaining things right. 

Like, I'll be talking about my overnight shift at the hospital—I'm an orderly, you know, just trying to help out—and then suddenly I'm talking about soccer, or the color of the paint on the walls, or patient charts. It just sort of tumbles out, and I can tell people are getting a bit lost. I really try to keep it all in a straight line, I promise, but it just gets a little jumbled. Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Lately, have you been feeling unusually energetic, like you need much less sleep than usual?

No, no, I don't think so. I mean, working the overnight shifts, my sleep is always a little weird anyway, but I definitely wouldn't say I'm energetic. If anything, I'm... well, I'm usually pretty tired. I try really hard to keep my energy up for the patients, but it's tough sometimes. I definitely don't feel like I need less sleep. I hope that's the right answer... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Is it okay that I'm just tired a lot?
Have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Um... I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining, because I know I'm lucky to have my job and everything. But... yeah, I guess I have been feeling a bit down. Actually, it's... most days I just feel really heavy, you know? And just kind of empty, right from the time I wake up. 

I try really hard to put on a good face for the patients, I promise I do. But sometimes, after my shifts are over... I'll just sit out in my car in the parking lot and cry for a while before I can even get it together to drive home. I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds pathetic. Is it okay that I'm telling you this? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right.
Have there been times when your thoughts or speech felt jumbled even when you were not feeling depressed?

Um, well... I hope I'm understanding the question right. There actually was a stretch of a few weeks where I wasn't in that really deep depressed place. I was trying so hard to be positive and do a good job, I promise. But my thoughts were still... well, they were still kind of tangled up. 

I'm a little embarrassed to admit this, so please don't think badly of me, but... during that time, I was just so sure that the security cameras at the hospital and all my supervisors were monitoring me. Like, watching my every single move to see if I'd mess up. So I kept acting really guarded at work, just trying to be perfectly careful. I guess my mind was still pretty mixed up with all of that, even though the sadness had lifted a little bit. Does that... does that answer what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Have you been diagnosed with a brain or nerve condition, like epilepsy, a head injury, or a brain infection?

Um, no, no sir. I haven't had anything like that. No seizures or head injuries or infections or anything. I've always been pretty healthy that way, physically speaking. I try to take good care of myself so I can be reliable at work. I hope that's the answer you were looking for... is it okay that I don't have any of those things? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information.
Did these suspicious thoughts and the jumbled speech start very suddenly, over a day or two?

Um, well... no, it wasn't sudden like that. I really wish I could say it was just a quick thing that came and went, but... it's actually been going on for a while. 

I'm really sorry, I probably should have mentioned this sooner, I just... I didn't want you to think I was completely losing my mind or that I couldn't do my job. But those feelings, like being watched and getting all mixed up in how I was acting... it's been happening for about a year and a month now. 

I've tried so hard to keep it under control and not let it show at work, I really have. I hope you don't think less of me for letting it go on that long without getting help. Is it... is it bad that it's been happening for that long? I'm just trying to be as honest as I can so you can help me.
